summary: E: CLAIMS.md:108 [shelf] XL reopen condition ('ride in the next Engine A candidate as extra raced arms') is met and the board has not moved (2.0352, blob d80df5ec); proceed as a user-requested below-bar stack. The XL half carries nearly all the value. The post-norm half is worth about 0.15-0.2% headline on the judge and will usually lose its 0.99-every-round bar.
justification: XL is plausible. It cuts per-record loop bookkeeping (SASS 617 -> 566 issued/record, a per-SM issue cut, which is the kind of change that transfers). It is bitwise E4/E5 (same loads, same order, same arithmetic) and was measured exact at every draw over 9 replicates. The E4/E5 landing transferred node consume-only 4-10% into judge kernel_fn E/m 0.955-0.965 (582bb334 log lines 118-122), and at 0.5-0.8x the XL consume gains of +1.4..+5.5% become about 1-2.5% per class. The probe's split bits match master's routes: v4xs at T<=16, v4cxs at 17..32/128/256, which agrees with the judge's [ea-enc] lines (T8/16 v4xs, T32/128/256 v4cxs). XL's run arithmetic (cnt0 = NK - (b & (NK-1)), flush at super-group end or e, setpass only at pass change) reproduces the master loop's flush points for any b/e, including cost-weighted splits, and master's body returns early on b >= e, so an empty CTA cannot reach XL's count-down loop with cnt 0. The `expected` list leaves out two rows XL also targets: verify_1 (T=8, E4XL 1.014-1.037) and verify_16 (T=128, E5XL 1.020-1.033). Add them. Weakest link 1: the port is not mechanical. patch_enc2.py anchors on the probe tree (eak::consume<DQ> with scale_enc/frag_a4b and dq 27/28 selected by `dq`). Master's E module is _eae_src4x(), which uses consume_e/ext_a4b/mul_bf16x2_h/scale_pair_imad_rt and selects E5 by pdl bit 4096 with ea['dq'] fixed at 2. So consume_lt has to be re-derived from master's consume_e, and XL needs a new pdl selector bit; check it against EA_PDL_BITS for collisions. Bitwise equality then holds only if the race's exact h/y gate passes. That gate exists (_eae_hy, NaN-poisoned) and must cover the XL arms. Weakest link 2: at T=256, XL only speeds up the cold half, which runs on the W6-M fork beside the hot half. The node had it off the critical path. On the judge, cold-iso E4 0.964 showed up as kernel_fn 0.975 (about 70%). The probe also measured T=256 on full routing, not on the hybrid's cold id set (experts with <= 16 routes), so the T=256 1.04-1.055 is an upper bound. The verify_32 gain is probably about 1-2% of the row. Post-norm swap: the hypothesis's x1.016 is the node figure. The glue note itself says the judge's SGLang post-norm is already 5.7 us, versus 9.95 on the node, and expects x1.008-1.011 on the row and about 0.15-0.2% headline. A <= 0.99 every-round bar against a ~0.99 true ratio with about ±0.3% round spread will mostly fail, so expect T=256 to stay on master's post-norm. The prior is right: the XL loop trim and X preload are new on top of the landed E4/E5. The probe found X null (E4X 0.99-1.02), so build only the XL instances. No do-not-try overlap: the refuted combine items (CLAIMS:39, cmbf) are Triton-on-Marlin and w2-epilogue fusion, not ea_combine at the T=256 tail, and ea_combine is already master's class-128 path. Build time: the [ea-enc] 4x module (4 kernels: E4/E5 x w13/w2) built in 52 s concurrently with ea4x 56 s, ea6 51 s and es1a 57 s. The join wait was 0.0 s and the phase started at 150 s against EAE_JOIN_S 220 from t0. Adding E4XL/E5XL x w13/w2 doubles that module's instantiations to 8, about 90-110 s under the same CPU contention. That still fits, but it eats about half the 70 s slack. Put the XL instances in their own module and thread ('4xl'), not in the 4x module, so a slow XL build is skipped and does not take E4/E5 down with it. The race grows from 1.8 s to about 4-5 s, well inside EAE_END_S 255. Size: 948,330 B plus consume_lt (~60 lines), the XL loop (~90 lines) and the race/selector glue comes to about +9-12 KB, roughly 960 KB, under 1,000,000 B. The post-norm swap reuses ea_combine, so it adds about 2-3 KB.
confounders: engine-a-a4b-a5b-encodings-race (landed, bbd1661f) + eae-cold-iso-keepalive-fix (f2b510f5): XL is built on the E4/E5 bank copies and the [ea-enc] race. Any XL reading is relative to the E arm the race would otherwise pick, so the per-class line must print XL/E4 and XL/E5 directly, not only XL/m. The keep-alive fix closed a prepare-only use-after-free in that same race. Adding arms and banks adds lifetimes, so the UAF class can come back (sticky illegal address = whole run fails, research/h100-glue-1029.md side finding).

v4x256c / W6-M fork (T=256 hybrid, hot half wh5ds on the fork stream): how much an XL cold-half gain is worth at T=256 depends on how much of the cold half sits on the critical path next to the hot half. A gain or loss at verify_32 can come from fork/hot-half overlap, not from XL. The isolated cold-half ratio the hypothesis already prints separates the two.

hothalf-wh-a5b-port (7da461db): it shortened the hot half, which pushes the cold half onto the critical path. This raises XL's T=256 payoff relative to the node (where the cold half was off-path), so expect judge > node at 256.

carrier (class-128 CUDA ea_combine) and the T=256 hybrid's join: the post-norm swap puts ea_combine with PDL right after a cross-stream event join. Its gain depends on which kernel is the programmatic predecessor (hot w2 on the capture stream) and on whether the cold half finishes last on that draw.

stack2 EPLF (fixed-role fix-up, T16): not a confounder on today's routes. The judge routes T=16 to v4xs (582bb334 log line 119), and _eae_base admits only v4x s twins, so XL never stacks with EPLF. If a route change put EPLF back at T16, XL would silently not apply there.
interference: No companion is needed. Both sub-changes are raced in-process against master with per-arm, per-round prints, and that race is the A/B. XL vs E4/E5 vs m comes per T class from the [ea-enc] lines (with the cold-iso ratio at 256). The post-norm swap is its own arm at T=256 through kernel_fn. A separate control run would only repeat what the prepare race measures on the same draws. The one ambiguity the race cannot settle is whether a verify_32 headline move comes from XL's cold half or from the post-norm swap. That can be split by having the T=256 race print the four cells {E, EXL} x {post-norm, ea_combine} rather than racing the two independently. This is a print requirement, not an extra judge run.
rules_flags: Post-norm swap is not bitwise. It is legal only through the fp32-reference tolerance gate. Use _ea_canary's rule: within half the judge's bounds (rel-L2 and worst row) and no worse than 2x master's error. Run it on the full T=256 hybrid path (hot + cold + ea_combine) on the p10/p50/p90 judge draws with NaN-poisoned outputs, plus one draw with extreme topk_weights. Fall back to master's post-norm on any failure. bs=257 / skewed tests never take this route (T == 256 only), so the canary is the only correctness evidence for it.

XL is admitted only on exact h/y equality to master in _eae_hy (poisoned buffers), at every draw, with err word 0 and tickets 0 after timing. Any mismatch means that arm is off. No tolerance is allowed for XL.

The race must stay in prepare, untimed, as today. No host sync or branching in kernel_fn. The routing is a fixed per-T selection. Nothing cached from timed inputs beyond the weight recode, which is already landed and legal.
freshness: CLAIMS.md:108 [shelf] E4XL/E5XL. Its reopen is 'ride in the next moe/decode Engine A candidate as extra raced arms (XL)', and this hypothesis is that, so it is met. A [shelf] mechanism proceeds only in a stack of >= 2.5% headline. This stack is about 1.5% (EV 0.75%), below the bar, and passes only as user_requested: true. Name it that way in the attempt file. CLAIMS.md:106 [landed] E4/E5 owns the same rows but is the base XL extends, not a competing mechanism. CLAIMS.md:111 [landed] keep-alive fix is the current master (f2b510f5). Board 2.0352 = BEST 575820c989c8412b, blob d80df5ec = mint blob, moved 0.00% against a 1.24% margin: fresh. The post-norm swap has no claim of its own. The glue note's own verdict is 'shelve as a rider for a T=256 stack', which this is. CLAIMS.md:112 [shelf] t128 hybrid + ea_combine is a different row (T=128) and is not stacked here, which is correct.
open_questions: Build must print: (1) [ea-enc] build per module with seconds, separate for 4x / 4xl / 6, plus join wait and phase-at time. (2) regs/lmem/occ for K1e4xl, K1e5xl, K2e4xl, K2e5xl. Gate each arm on lmem 0 and occ 2. The probe read 92-94 regs on cu13.0, close to the 96 cap of __launch_bounds__(THREADS, 2), so a different nvcc on the judge could spill. (3) Per class T=8/16/32/128/256: exact h/y per arm, E/m per round for m/E4/E5/E4XL/E5XL, and the direct XL/E ratio. (4) At T=256: cold-iso ratios for all four E arms, the {E, EXL} x {post-norm, ea_combine} kernel_fn cells, and the canary rel-L2 / worst row of ea_combine vs master's. (5) PATH CHOSEN per T. (6) submission size in bytes.

Selection rule among several passing arms: the race picks on worst round today. With XL vs E4 differing by about 1-2% and a round spread of about ±1%, say whether ties (|XL/E - 1| < 0.5%) default to the incumbent E arm, which is the safer choice.

At T=256 the probe showed E5 beats E4 consume-only by 1-2.6%, yet the judge picked E4 at 256 (582bb334: kernel_fn E4 0.975 vs E5 0.980, cold iso 0.964 vs 0.961). Race E4XL and E5XL both at 256. Do not pre-select E5XL from the node numbers.

Post-norm bar: a true judge ratio of about 0.99 against a <= 0.99 every-round bar will mostly fail. Either accept that the post-norm half is likely a no-op (fine, about 0.2% at most) or gate it on mean <= 0.995 with worst <= 1.000. Decide before the run, not after reading it.

Verify that the 4xl module's pdl selector bit does not collide with existing EA_PDL_BITS (256, 512, 4096, EA4C_CW << 4) and that _eae_info / ok{} are widened from 4 to 8 rows. Today they are hard-coded to K1e4/K1e5/K2e4/K2e5.
